### A1. RA 6713, the Code of Conduct

**Text (lawphil):**

- **§3(i):** "'Conflict of interest' arises when a public official or employee is a member of a board, an officer, or a substantial stockholder of a private corporation or owner or has a substantial interest in a business, and the interest of such corporation or business, or his rights or duties therein, may be opposed to or affected by the faithful performance of official duty."
- **§7(a):** "Public officials and employees shall not, directly or indirectly, have any financial or material interest in any transaction requiring the approval of their office."
- **§8(A):** officials "shall file under oath their Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth … and those of their spouses and unmarried children under eighteen (18) years of age living in their households," covering "(a) real property, its improvements, acquisition costs, assessed value and current fair market value".
- **§4(A)(c):** officials "shall not dispense or extend undue favors on account of their office to their relatives whether by consanguinity or affinity".

**Elements against the record:**

- **§3(i) conflict of interest.** Its definition concerns interests in a private corporation or business. The record shows no business interest of Erwin's. **Does not fit.**
- **§7(a).** This needs (1) a transaction requiring his office's approval and (2) a financial or material interest of his in it.
  - The record shows no transaction approved by the Municipal Engineer's office: no building permit, no occupancy permit, no MEO endorsement on the plan.
  - It shows no interest of Erwin's in the lot.
  - **Does not fit on the record.** It could fit only if permits for the structures were issued by his office and he has an interest [evidence missing].
- **§8 SALN disclosure.** It covers the official's own property and that of the spouse and unmarried children under 18. A parent's lot is not within §8.
  - The record shows no interest of Erwin's in TCT 079-2021002126 (PEC p.1).
  - **Does not fit.** Unless Erwin holds an undisclosed interest [no record fact].
- **§4(A)(c) undue favors to relatives.** This needs an official act. The record shows none.
  - Requesting RD certified copies is a public counter service: the copies were paid for, with an official receipt (DX1; DX6). It is not an act of his office.
  - **Does not fit.**

**Evidence missing (not to be gathered for this purpose without the CoS):**

- building and occupancy permits for the structures on the lot, and the approving office;
- whether the Mercedes Municipal Engineer is the designated Building Official (PB §4 asserts it) [VERIFY];
- Erwin's appointment date;
- any MEO document in the 2020–2021 subdivision or tax-declaration chain.

### A2. RA 3019 §3, the Anti-Graft Act (only the subsections that could touch the facts)

**Text (lawphil):**

- **§3(e):** "Causing any undue injury to any party, including the Government, or giving any private party any unwarranted benefits, advantage or preference in the discharge of his official administrative or judicial functions through manifest partiality, evident bad faith or gross inexcusable negligence. This provision shall apply to officers and employees of offices or government corporations charged with the grant of licenses or permits or other concessions."
- **§3(h):** "Director [sic: lawphil text] or indirectly having financing or pecuniary interest in any business, contract or transaction in connection with which he intervenes or takes part in his official capacity, or in which he is prohibited by the Constitution or by any law from having any interest."
- **§3(j):** "Knowingly approving or granting any license, permit, privilege or benefit in favor of any person not qualified for or not legally entitled to such license, permit, privilege or advantage …"
- **§11** (lawphil text): "All offenses punishable under this Act shall prescribe in ten years." [UNVERIFIED: a later amendment to fifteen years by RA 10910 was not read.]

**Elements against the record:**

- **§3(e).** It needs (1) a public officer (fits: JA-E S3), (2) acting "in the discharge of his official administrative … functions", (3) manifest partiality, evident bad faith or gross inexcusable negligence, and (4) undue injury or unwarranted benefit.
  - Element (2) has no record fact. CMP ¶35 alleges it, but no exhibit shows an official act.
  - **Does not fit on the record.**
- **§3(h).** It needs a pecuniary interest plus intervention in his official capacity. Neither appears. **Does not fit.**
- **§3(j).** It needs a license or permit he approved. None is in the record. **Does not fit** [evidence missing: permits].
- **§3(a), (b), (c), (d), (f), (g), (i), (k).** No record fact touches gifts, employment, contracts with government, boards, or confidential information. **Not analysed.**

### A4. Ombudsman jurisdiction (RA 6770)

**Text (lawphil):**

- **§15(1):** "Investigate and prosecute on its own or on complaint by any person, any act or omission of any public officer or employee, office or agency, when such act or omission appears to be illegal, unjust, improper or inefficient."
- **§16:** "The provisions of this Act shall apply to all kinds of malfeasance, misfeasance, and non-feasance that have been committed by any officer or employee as mentioned in Section 13 hereof, during his tenure of office."
- **§20:** "The Office of the Ombudsman may not conduct the necessary investigation of any administrative act or omission complained of if it believes that: (1) The complainant has an adequate remedy in another judicial or quasi-judicial body; (2) The complaint pertains to a matter outside the jurisdiction of the Office of the Ombudsman; (3) The complaint is trivial, frivolous, vexatious or made in bad faith; (4) The complainant has no sufficient personal interest in the subject matter of the grievance; or (5) The complaint was filed after one (1) year from the occurrence of the act or omission complained of."

**Application:**

- **Jurisdiction over the person.** Erwin is a public officer, so the Ombudsman has jurisdiction over his person (§§13, 15(1), 21).
- **§16 tenure.** Any act must be "during his tenure of office". His start date is not in the record [gap]. If he took office after Sep 2020–Nov 2021, the alleged survey and title acts fall outside it [CONDITIONAL].
- **§20(5) one-year rule.** For administrative complaints: the survey (8 Sep 2020), plan approval (6 Apr 2021), title (23 Nov 2021) and ARP (27 Jul 2023) are each more than one year old. The 2026 certified-copy requests are recent, but they are not official acts.
  - The text says "may not", which reads as discretionary [INFERRED; no case read].
  - §20(5) does not apply to criminal complaints under RA 3019 (see §11 prescription).
- **§20(1).** 26-360 is pending on the same allegations (CMP ¶¶11, 35). The Ombudsman may treat it as an "adequate remedy".

### A6. Risk to 26-360 and recommendation

**Risk:**

- **Erwin's defense in 26-360.** His First Affirmative Defense is that he is sued for being a public officer without any act (ANS ¶37). An administrative complaint built on the same allegation, without new facts, supports his narrative and the counterclaim.
- **Two forums, one allegation.** Parallel proceedings on CMP ¶35 invite inconsistent findings. The certification against forum shopping is a Rule 7 matter [VERIFY applicability; the causes of action differ].
- **Mixing with the ARTA track.** Mixing this with the separate ARTA/CSC track risks the "retaliation" reading.

**Recommendation:**

- **Never**, on the present record.
- **After judgment**, re-examine only if the permits subpoena (PB §6.2), returned in 26-360, shows an approval by his office of structures on this lot. Even then, only through counsel and only on a document-level fact.
- Keep cross-examination in 26-360 as the only present use (dossier 5.5).
